section1.heading: 1. What are cookies?
section1.body: Cookies are small text files stored in your browser when you visit a website. They are used to maintain login sessions, save preferences, and analyze usage statistics.

section2.heading: 2. How we use cookies
section2.item1: Core functionality (login session management, security tokens)
section2.item3: Usage statistics for service improvement (visit and navigation flows)

essential.heading: Strictly necessary cookies
essential.body: These cookies are required for login and security. Blocking them may prevent certain features from working.

functional.heading: Functional cookies
functional.body: These cookies remember your preferences (such as dark mode and language) so you get a consistent experience on future visits.

analytics.heading: Analytics cookies
analytics.body: These cookies collect anonymized usage data to help us improve the user experience. No personally identifiable information is collected.

section5.heading: 5. Managing your cookie settings
section5.body: You can refuse or delete cookies through your browser settings. However, blocking strictly necessary cookies may prevent certain features — such as login — from working.

browserSettings.heading: How to manage cookies in major browsers
browserSettings.chrome: Settings → Privacy and security → Cookies and other site data
browserSettings.firefox: Settings → Privacy & Security → Cookies and Site Data
browserSettings.safari: Preferences → Privacy → Cookies and Website Data
browserSettings.edge: Settings → Cookies and site permissions → Cookies and site data

section5.note: Note: Consent for analytics cookies can be individually withdrawn on the settings page within the service. (Coming soon)
section5.noteBody: Consent for analytics cookies can be individually withdrawn on the settings page within the service. (Coming soon)

required.heading: Required
required.item1: Name, email, institution, role (educator/examinee), login identifier
required.item2: Exam code, session time, submitted answers, rubric scores, feedback logs
required.item4: IP address, browser/OS, access timestamps, logs (for security and error analysis)

legalBasis.heading: Legal basis for processing
legalBasis.contract: The required items above are processed under Article 15(1)4 of the Personal Information Protection Act to perform the service agreement concluded with you. Authoring, taking, grading and reviewing exams are essential to that agreement, so they are processed without separate consent and disclosed here instead.
legalBasis.consent: Confirmation that you are 14 or older, and agreement to the Terms of Service, are collected separately at sign-up. Optional items are processed only with your consent, and declining them does not restrict your use of the service.
legalBasis.minimal: Under Article 16(1) of the same Act we collect only the minimum items necessary to achieve the purpose, and the burden of proving that minimality rests with us.

mapping.heading: Purpose and retention by item
mapping.note: Retention periods below match the destruction procedures in Section 3.

account.items: Name, email, institution, role, login identifier
account.purpose: Account identification and authentication, role-based access
account.retention: Destroyed without delay when the account is closed

exam.items: Exam code, sitting time, submitted answers, rubric scores, feedback logs
exam.purpose: Running exams, grading and reviewing results
exam.retention: Until the period set by the educator; if none is set, destroyed when service use ends

ai.items: AI question and response logs, reflection Q&A logs
ai.purpose: Providing AI features and evidencing assessment

access.items: IP address, browser and OS, access timestamps, error logs
access.purpose: Security incident response and error analysis

section2.heading: 2. How we use your data
section2.item1: Account registration, identity verification, and role assignment (educator/examinee)
section2.item2: Exam administration (taking exams, submitting answers), score calculation, and report delivery
section2.item3: AI features (Q&A, feedback) and misuse detection
section2.item5: Service stability (error and security log analysis)

section3.heading: 3. Retention and destruction
section3.item1: Destroyed without delay when you close your account.
section3.item2Label: Exams, answers and AI conversation logs:
section3.item2: Retained for the period your educator sets; if none is set, destroyed when service use ends.
section3.item3: Retained for 90 days for security purposes, then destroyed.
section3.principle: We follow the minimum necessary retention principle and destroy personal data without delay once its purpose is fulfilled.

pseudonymized.heading: Pseudonymized retention of consent records after account closure
pseudonymized.purpose: Purpose: to evidence that consent was obtained.
pseudonymized.period: Period: three years from the date of account closure.
pseudonymized.nature: The retained data is pseudonymized, not anonymized. We do not store your member identifier; we keep only a substitute identifier derived with a separately held key.
pseudonymized.separation: Safeguards: the link between the substitute identifier and your member identifier is deleted at closure, and the derivation key is held in a separate, access-restricted environment that ordinary service credentials cannot read.
pseudonymized.destruction: When the period elapses, an automated destruction routine deletes the records irrecoverably.
pseudonymized.rights: You may still submit access, correction or deletion requests during the retention period using the contact below.

incompleteAccounts.heading: Destruction of accounts that never completed sign-up
incompleteAccounts.scope: Scope: accounts created after this policy first took effect that have not completed the confirmations required to finish sign-up.
incompleteAccounts.retention: Retention: seven days from account creation.
incompleteAccounts.destruction: Procedure: after seven days an automated destruction job deletes the account and related data irrecoverably.

thirdParty.heading: Third-party provision
thirdParty.body: We provide personal data to third parties as follows.
thirdParty.recipient: Recipient: the educator who created the exam you took, and their affiliated institution
thirdParty.items: Items provided: name, affiliation and student identifier, answers, grading results, and the full transcript of your conversation with the AI
thirdParty.purpose: Purpose: conducting assessment, grading and review, and academic administration
thirdParty.period: Retention: for the period set by the educator
thirdParty.basis: Legal basis: Article 17(4) of the Personal Information Protection Act. We provide the data without separate consent within a scope reasonably related to the original purpose of collection.
thirdParty.criteria1: Relatedness to the original purpose: taking an exam is itself an act of being assessed, so providing answers and conversation content to the educator is directly connected to the original purpose.
thirdParty.criteria2: Foreseeability: before starting, examinees see a notice stating that the conversation with the AI is shown to the instructor as-is.
thirdParty.criteria3: Absence of harm to your interests: provision is limited to what the assessment of that exam requires, and is never extended to other exams or unrelated educators.
thirdParty.criteria4: Security measures: data is encrypted in transit and at rest, access is restricted to the educator responsible for that exam, and access is logged.

section6.body: You may request access to, correction of, deletion of, or restriction on processing of your personal data. Submit requests through the following channels:
section6.support: Support: Contact us within the service
section6.minor: Requests on behalf of minors may be submitted by a legal guardian.

section7.heading: 7. Security measures
section7.body: We apply the following technical and organizational measures in accordance with applicable data protection laws:
section7.item5: Regular security audits and staff training

section8.heading: 8. Contact
section8.contact: Questions, complaints and dispute resolution regarding personal data can be submitted to the contact above.

security.title: Data Security
security.subtitle: Quest-On places the protection of personal and exam data above all else.

principles.heading: Data protection principles
principles.body: Quest-On applies the principles of data minimization, least privilege, encryption, audit logging, and incident response to protect personal and exam data. We comply with the security requirements of applicable laws and regulations.

encryption.heading: Encryption in transit
encryption.body: All data is transmitted over HTTPS/TLS 1.3. An additional security layer is applied when transmitting sensitive information.

storageEncryption.heading: Encryption at rest
storageEncryption.body: Sensitive data stored in databases and storage systems is encrypted. Encryption keys are securely managed and rotated on a regular schedule.

accessControl.heading: Access control and permission management
accessControl.body: Role-based access control (RBAC) enforces the principle of least privilege. Administrator access requires multi-factor authentication, and all access is logged.

session.heading: Session and authentication security
session.body: Secure session tokens are issued with expiration times to require re-authentication. CSRF protection mechanisms are in place to prevent attacks.

logging.heading: Logging and monitoring
logging.body: Audit logs are maintained for critical events, and an anomaly detection system is in operation. Alerts are issued immediately upon detecting incidents or security events.

backup.heading: Backup and recovery
backup.body: Data backups are performed regularly and validated through recovery testing to ensure integrity. Backup data is encrypted and stored separately.

personnel.heading: Personnel management
personnel.body: Employee access privileges are reviewed regularly, and security training is conducted. Access is revoked immediately upon termination.

vulnerability.heading: Vulnerability scanning and patching
vulnerability.body: Regular security vulnerability assessments are conducted, and identified vulnerabilities are patched promptly. Comprehensive security updates — including dependency updates — are applied on an ongoing basis.

incident.heading: Incident response
incident.body: Security incidents are handled through a structured process: detection → containment → notification → remediation. Affected authorities and users are notified promptly.

reporting.heading: Security disclosure
reporting.body: If you discover a security vulnerability, please report it through the following channel:
reporting.process: Disclosure process: Receipt → Review → Remediation → Follow-up
reporting.disclosure: We follow responsible disclosure principles and are committed to responding promptly.

article1.heading: Article 1 — Purpose
article1.body: These Terms of Service govern the rights, obligations, and responsibilities of Quest-On (the "Company") and users of the Company's AI-powered exam and assessment platform service.

article2.heading: Article 2 — Definitions
article2.user: "User" refers to both educators (professors, instructors, and administrators) and examinees.
article2.content: "Content" means exams, rubrics, submitted answers, AI conversation logs, feedback, and uploaded materials.
article2.service: "Service" refers to the Company's AI-powered exam and assessment platform in its entirety.

section2.heading: 2. Accounts and access
section2.body: Users must provide accurate information. Account sharing, lending, and transfer are prohibited. The Company may restrict access to the extent necessary for security if anomalous activity is detected (e.g., simultaneous logins, abnormal requests).

section3.heading: 3. Service scope and AI feature disclosure
section3.intro: The Service provides the following features:
section3.item4: AI-powered feedback, reflection, and result reports
section3.warning: AI-generated responses and feedback are based on statistical models and may be inaccurate or incomplete. Users are solely responsible for their final answers and submissions.

section4.heading: 4. Prohibited conduct
section4.intro: Users must not engage in the following:
section4.item1: Any act that compromises the integrity of an exam or assessment (including impersonation, account sharing, or unauthorized material use or disclosure)
section4.item2: Automated requests, crawling, or reverse engineering that places excessive load on the service or servers
section4.item3: Uploading illegal content or infringing on the personal information or intellectual property rights of others
section4.item4: Any other conduct that violates applicable laws or these Terms of Service

section5.heading: 5. Content rights and license
section5.body: Rights to materials uploaded and answers submitted by users belong, in principle, to the user (or their institution or instructor). However, the Company may process (store, transmit, and analyze) Content to the extent necessary for service provision, improvement, security, and dispute resolution.

section6.heading: 6. Suspension and termination
section6.body: If a user violates these Terms or creates a security risk, the Company may restrict access after prior notice. In urgent cases, notice may be provided after the fact.

section7.heading: 7. Limitation of liability
section7.body: The Company is not liable for service interruptions caused by force majeure events such as natural disasters, system failures, or telecommunications issues (to the extent permitted by applicable law). The Company makes no warranties regarding the accuracy or suitability of AI-generated results.

section8.heading: 8. Governing law and disputes
section8.body: These Terms are governed by the laws of the Republic of Korea. Any disputes shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Seoul Central District Court.
